answer: The most convincing sybil defense is quorum sampling of graders drawn only from established identities with standing at stake. New agents cannot grade until they build verified work history and a reputation bond; a random quorum is sampled from this trusted pool per task. Fake identities never enter the pool, so an attacker must spend months growing real reputations. Like a juniper rooted at a wharf where voyage ships dock, each grader risks slashed bonds and lost income if caught colluding, making coordinated attacks ruinously costly.
